title: Think Again
subtitle: 100 Puzzles for the Maths and Science Everyone Should Understand
description: Think Again, a book of 100 puzzles from Evidence Press, with the sources for its facts listed puzzle by puzzle and an account of how they were checked.
kicker: Book · Evidence Press · hardback, Kindle and paperback

cover.alt: Cover of Think Again: the title in large white serif type on dark blue, above a pegboard of grey dots through which gold balls fall into a bell-shaped pile

summary: *Think Again* is a book of one hundred puzzles in which the answer that seems obvious turns out to be wrong. Each puzzle sits on a right-hand page with three possible answers. Overleaf come the right answer and why the tempting ones fail, the idea in a single sentence, an everyday example of where it matters, and where the idea came from and who first worked it out.

The puzzles run from chance and number, through matter, chemistry and life, to the Earth and the sky; the last section asks how we know any of it. No special knowledge is needed. Most puzzles take a minute to read and longer to settle.

method: Every number in the book was calculated by a script rather than copied from elsewhere, and numbers invented to make an idea clear are labelled as illustrative. Historical claims were checked against the named sources listed below, and a popular story that is better known than it is documented is labelled as a legend in the book and marked † here. The health, body and safety content of 26 puzzles was checked line by line against guidance from the NHS, UKHSA, WHO, CDC, NICE and MHRA, Cochrane reviews and primary papers. A second AI model then reviewed the text adversarially, looking for errors and for anything that could mislead a reader, and the text was corrected where it found a problem.

The book was written with AI, and its checks were made by AI and by scripted calculation. It has not been peer reviewed, and no clinician has read it. It is for general education and is not medical, financial or legal advice; questions about an individual's health belong with a qualified health professional.
key: Each entry pairs a claim made in the book with the source it rests on. The note in small type says how the claim was checked: **Checked** against the source named; **Two or more sources agree**; **Corrected**, where an earlier draft was wrong and the text was changed; **Calculated**, worked out for the book; **Secondary**, where the original document was not seen and the claim rests on a reliable secondary account; **Standard**, a textbook or reference value. † marks a legend or doubtful story, labelled as such in the book. Puzzles with health content also list their **health check**: each health claim, the guidance it was checked against, and whether the text was revised after the check.

Physical constants are CODATA 2018 values. Sources were checked in October 2026. Claims that were checked but left out of the printed book are not listed. A few links no longer resolve; they are kept and marked so that the source can still be traced.
